sections.title: The big picture
sections.lede: Describe your day with separable verbs and three small time words.

blocks.text: Separable verbs have a prefix that moves to the end of a main clause: aufstehen becomes Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf. The conjugated verb stays in second position and the prefix waits at the end.

Use um for clock times (um sieben Uhr), am for days and parts of the day (am Montag, am Morgen), and im for months and seasons (im Januar, im Sommer). These prepositions do not change the noun after them.

blocks.title: The prefix is not optional
blocks.text: In a main clause, the prefix must go to the end. "Ich aufstehe um sieben" is not German.

sections.title: Rules & patterns
sections.lede: The patterns to keep in mind while you work through the examples.

rows: Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.
Der Kurs beginnt um neun Uhr.

items: The prefix goes to the very end of the main clause.
Use am with days: am Montag, am Wochenende.
Use im with months and seasons: im Mai, im Winter.

sections.title: Pronunciation
sections.lede: Short, focused sound work. Play each item and repeat it twice.

blocks.text: Many German workplaces start early, and "Feierabend" is the everyday word for the end of the working day. Shops in smaller towns may close earlier than in big cities, and Sunday remains a quiet day for most retail.
Mealtimes vary by region and family. "Frühstück" can be a full meal with bread, cheese and coffee, while "Abendbrot" is often a light evening meal rather than a cooked dinner.

sections.title: Speaking
sections.lede: Record or say your answer aloud, then compare it with the model.
sections.prompt: Describe your morning in three sentences. Use one separable verb and one time phrase.

model.de: Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf. Am Morgen trinke ich Kaffee. Dann kaufe ich ein.
model.en: I get up at seven. In the morning I drink coffee. Then I shop.

tips: Start with "Ich stehe … auf" and put the prefix at the end.
Use am for parts of the day and um for clock times.
Connect your sentences with dann or danach to sound more fluent.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.lede: These are the errors learners most often make with this pattern.

items.why: The conjugated verb must be in second position, with the prefix at the end.
The time phrase comes before the final prefix.

items.wrong: Am acht Uhr beginnt der Kurs.
items.right: Um acht Uhr beginnt der Kurs.
items.why: Clock times use um, not am.
